title: Maleah Joi Moon on Netflix’s ‘A Different World,’ Debbie Allen’s Backstage Offer and Owning the Show’s ‘Complicated History’ With Cosby
full_text: × Nov 20, 2026 9:40am PT Maleah Joi Moon on Netflix’s ‘A Different World,’ Debbie Allen’s Backstage Offer and Owning the Show’s ‘Complicated History’ With Cosby By Clayton Davis Plus Icon Clayton Davis Chief Awards Editor byClaytonDavis Latest Two Directors, One Oscar: Can Lord and Miller, Los Javis, Fielder and Oppenheim or the Esiri Brothers Break Through? 17 hours ago Oscar Predictions: Costume Design — Will the Academy Embrace the Three Distinct Eras of ‘La Bola Negra’? 18 hours ago Sequels, Subtitles and Spring Releases: How the Best Picture Race Is Rewriting the Academy’s Playbook 22 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source ELI ADE/Netflix Maleah Joi Moon didn’t audition her way into Hillman College. Debbie Allen walked backstage at “Hell’s Kitchen,” held the Tony winner’s face in her hands and decided she had found the daughter of Whitley Gilbert and Dwayne Wayne. “She’s never been apologetic about letting me know my light,” Moon says of Allen, the choreographer, director and producer who shaped the original TV series “ A Different World ” and now shepherds Netflix ’s sequel comedy, which is eligible in this season’s Golden Globes race. “She’s a tree to me, and I know that sounds kind of woo-woo, but it means she’s so sturdy.” Related Stories 'Unzipped' 4K Restoration to Make Streaming Debut on Criterion Channel (EXCLUSIVE) Jane Fonda 'Didn't Dare Imagine' Democrats' Blue Tsunami: 'We Have to Block What's Bad and Fight For What's Good' The call came the weekend before Moon left the Alicia Keys musical. There was no Zoom or pleasantries. “She gets straight to the point,” Moon says. Moon plays Deborah, the daughter of the sitcom’s beloved couple; the casting carries a full-circle weight for her own family. Her mother immigrated from Belize, and her father grew up in the Bronx. Neither came from a world where kids went off to college, which is precisely why the original series hit so hard. “You see these young, Black, stylish, joyful, well-educated, pursuing academia young people and she had that same feeling that everybody else had in the world when they saw the 1980s version,” says Moon. Building Deborah started in the writers’ room, where showrunner Felicia Pride invited Moon to talk through her own life story. The first relationship she built was the one with Whitley. Rewatching Jasmine Guy’s performance as an actor, not just as a fan, Moon found more than comic timing. “I saw somebody who was strong-willed, somebody who was outspoken, ambitious and not afraid to be who she is, which is huge for a Black woman,” she says. “I know so much of who I am is my mom living inside of me.” Guy and Kadeem Hardison, back as Whitley and Dwayne, were generous with on-set wisdom. Hardison taught her to count her steps to her mark; Guy called and talked for two hours at a stretch. Both preach the same gospel: take care of yourself. “When outside influences are coming in to say who they think you are,” Moon says, “[Guy] inspires me to remember who the fuck I am.” Moon, who is queer, is equally passionate about Amir, played by Jordan Herron Hall, the franchise’s first openly queer character. She frames him as a person who happens to be queer rather than a queer character. “Black love in all forms, in the sexuality sense, in the gender sense, in the community sense, in the familial sense, in the self-sense, is Black radicalism,” she says. “That is our game changer.” With a Tony and a Grammy already on the shelf, Moon is now focusing on music, her first love before acting or dance. She’s been in the studio workshopping what her sound might be, and she’s signed on to projects she can’t yet name. A “Hell’s Kitchen” film? She’d audition for Keys all over again. A Broadway return? “Hadestown,” where her friend Amber Iman is currently starring, is on her wish list. One piece of the Hillman inheritance is harder to celebrate. The original “A Different World” was born as a spinoff of “The Cosby Show,” and Moon doesn’t pretend otherwise. “We know that there is a complicated history. We’re not going to beat around the bush,” she says. The two shows “have their own fortitude, like they have their own legacies, both of them,” Moon says. “As much as they are interlinked, it’s so wonderful that they both stand on their own.” Her prayer is that the Netflix version earns the same footing. “No matter what that conversation looks like, the point is that we are telling a story of love that was born in its genesis from ‘The Cosby Show’ and has continued through this generational re-embarking of another story and another story and another story,” she says. “That is how love is passed down. Period.” See all Academy Awards predictions Variety Awards Circuit: Oscars Bond Girl Lea Seydoux Says ‘I Don’t Really Care’ Who Becomes 007’s New Female Lead: ‘It’s Become American’ Now Ben Affleck Raved About Robert Pattinson’s ‘The Odyssey’ Performance, Recalls Matt Damon: He Said ‘It Was Like Watching a Guy Run Into an Avalanche’ Robert Pattinson Was Bribed to Star in ‘Primetime’ With 200 Zyn Canisters and a Note That Read: ‘Dear Chris Han-Zyn’ Robert Pattinson Praises Steven Soderbergh for Stepping in to Finish ‘Batman 2’ Filming for Matt Reeves: ‘Completely Selfless’ Pierce Brosnan Approves of Callum Turner as James Bond: He’s ‘So Strong’ and I’m ‘Eager to See’ Who Becomes the Next 007 Robert Pattinson Says ‘Batman 2’ Filming Will ‘Pause for a Little Bit’ After Director Matt Reeves Steps Away: ‘We’re Going to Figure It All Out’ Loading comments...

title: Kristin Chenoweth to Honor Late Dolly Parton With Gay Men’s Chorus of Los Angeles at Holiday Shows
full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All November 20, 2026 9:34am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Kristin Chenoweth attends A New York Evening Celebrating Peggy Lee presented by the Grammy Museum at the Arnhold Center at 92NY in New York on June 12, 2023. (Photo by Rob Kim/Getty Images for The Recording Academy) The Gay Men’s Chorus of Los Angeles will honor the late Dolly Parton at back-to-back holiday concerts next month and the group has recruited a very special guest to join and pay respects through song. Emmy and Tony Award winner Kristin Chenoweth will hit the stage with GMCLA for A Very Dolly Holiday!, which will take place Dec. 12 and 13 at Saban Theatre in Beverly Hills, Calif. The chorus, which is kicking off its 48th season, will honor the iconic Parton by performing some of her hits and beloved favorites like “Coat of Many Colors,” “I Will Always Love You,” “Light of a Clear Blue Morning,” “Islands in the Stream,” “Hard Candy Christmas” and “9 to 5” along with holiday favorites like “Happy Xmas,” “Where Are You Christmas?,” “O Holy Night,” “The Christmas Song” and “Let It Snow.” Related Stories Music Dolly Parton Lands Three Posthumous Grammy Nominations Lifestyle Hollywood's Latest Must-Have Luxury? Listening Rooms “Kristin Chenoweth is one of the great theatrical and vocal talents of our time, a true ally to our community, and someone we’ve been hoping to welcome for quite some time,” said executive director and producer Lou Spisto. “We are absolutely thrilled to have her join us, particularly now, as I can’t imagine a more perfect occasion than A Very Dolly Holiday! Kristin’s deep affection for Dolly Parton, both as an artist and as a person, makes this collaboration especially meaningful. To have a Broadway legend join us in celebrating the ultimate icon and sharing the joy, love and spirit that Dolly represents is something truly special.” Said Chenoweth: “Celebrating my queen Dolly Parton with the Gay Men’s Chorus of Los Angeles? It just doesn’t get any better. I’ve been a fan of the chorus forever, and I’m so excited to get to take the stage with these fabulous men for the first time. We’re going to give the audiences a show they won’t forget.” Most recently, Chenoweth, best known for a range of roles from Wicked to Pushing Daisies, most recently produced and starred in Broadway’s The Queen of Versailles . She can be seen on the upcoming fifth season of Peacock’s The Traitors. Tickets are available here . GMCLA’s nearly 200-voice chorus is under the leadership of artistic director Ernest H. Harrison. THR

title: ‘Presumed Innocent’ Season 2 Pairs Rachel Brosnahan With Matthew Rhys in First Look at Next Courtroom Face-Off
full_text: Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All November 20, 2026 9:32am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Presumed Innocent' season two: Matthew Rhys and Rachel Brosnahan. Apple TV Logo text Matthew Rhys and Rachel Brosnan are a married couple in court — but not for a divorce — in the first look teaser for Apple TV ’s Presumed Innocent second season to premiere Feb. 19, 2027. The Emmy award winners are legal eagles clashing over a murder case in the anthology series’ sophomore season. Brosnahan plays up-and-coming defense attorney Lelia Reynolds facing off in court against her district attorney husband, played by Rhys, in a murder case that threatens to destroy both their careers and their marriage, according to a synopsis from the producers. Related Stories Business Apple TV Bulks Up With Video Podcasts TV 'Slow Horses' Lands Early Renewal for Seasons 9 and 10 at Apple TV The first season of Presumed Innocent was based on Scott Turow’s novel of the same name (previously adapted for a feature film starring Harrison Ford) and starred Jake Gyllenhaal, Ruth Negga and Peter Sarsgaard. In renewing the show , Apple TV+ and the show’s creative team, which includes executive producers David E. Kelley and J.J. Abrams, opted to make the series an anthology. Apple TV is keeping plot details about season two mostly under wraps. Publisher Pan Macmillan’s description of Dissection of a Murder says the story will follow an attorney (Brosnahan) who is defending a man accused of murdering a judge. Courtney B. Vance and Fiona Shaw also feature in the short teaser for the Emmy Award-nominated drama based on Dissection of a Murder legal thriller novel by Jo Murray. The second season ensemble cast includes Jack Reynor, Lesley-Ann Brandt and Judith Light as a guest star. That star casting isn’t surprising as Presumed Innocent , from showrunner David E. Kelley and executive producer J.J. Abrams, during its first season earned Emmy nominations for Gyllenhaal, Bill Camp, Sarsgaard and Negga in varied acting categories. Brosnahan is known for her Emmy-winning star turn on The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel, while Rhys stars in Apple’s popular Widow’s Bay comedy, about the residents of a seemingly cursed New England seaside town, and earned two lead acting awards at this year’s Emmy Awards. Kelley, Abrams share executive producer credits on Presumed Innocent season two with Rachel Rusch Rich, Dee Johnson, Dustin Thomason, Brosnahan, Scott Turow and Gyllenhaal, after he starred in the first season. The opening two episodes will debut on Feb. 19, with weekly releases to follow until April 2. THR

title: Hollywood’s Top 25 Legal Troubleshooters
full_text: Skip to main content Legal Eagles D4vd was flanked by attorneys Blair Berk (left) and Marilyn Bednarski. Ted Soqui — Pool/Getty Images Logo text In Hollywood, having a lawyer on speed dial can mean only one of two things. A deal is imminent, or a jury is deliberating. If it’s the latter, chances are the attorney on the other end of the line is on this list. The 25 Legal Troubleshooters on these pages handle the problems agents can’t negotiate away: criminal charges, custody fights, contested fortunes and who gets to sell the Lakers. Their firms represent stars, moguls and heirs, although lately the L.A. Public Defender’s Office has been giving them unexpected competition. The lawyers themselves are attracting attention, too. Brian Steel has a Drake song named after him; Laura Wasser has a fashion campaign. Others spend their days explaining why a chatbot shouldn’t rewrite your trust. All are worth keeping in your contacts. Just in case. Marc Agnifilo, Karen Friedman Agnifilo and Teny Geragos Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject (3) Logo text Agnifilo Intrater LLP Criminal Defense Litigation This firmspent the year representing famous clients facing charges of murder, rape and sex trafficking. Agnifilo and Geragos followed their defense of Sean “Diddy” Combs with Harvey Weinstein’s third trial, which ended in a hung jury, while another client, Oren Alexander, Kim Kardashian’s former real estate broker, was convicted of sex trafficking alongside brothers Tal and Alon. (Tal was represented by Deanna Paul, now a partner at Geragos & Geragos.) Friedman Agnifilo, meanwhile, helped take the death penalty off the table for Luigi Mangione, then pressed to dismiss his state murder case on double jeopardy grounds following his federal plea. But the firm’s most incendiary client this year has nothing to do with Hollywood: Winston Lee is one of seven former Cornell fraternity members accused in a civil suit of drugging and gang-raping a fellow student. Patrick Baghdaserians Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Baghdaserians Law Group Inc. Family Law Litigation Actor Olivier Martinez had Baghdaserians in his corner during his headline-grabbing custody battle with ex-wife Halle Berry. In October, the lawyer secured a temporary restraining order and primary physical custody of their 13-year-old son. The judge later dissolved the restraining order but kept Martinez the primary custodial parent. Martinez is now seeking increased child support and $240,000 in legal fees from Berry. Another custody client: Basketball Wives ’ Clayanna Warthen, whose dispute involved former NBA player Andre Iguodala. Blair Berk Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Berk Brettler LLP Criminal Defense Litigation Berk’s clients sit on both sides of criminal cases: She has represented stalking victim Jennifer Aniston and defended Harvey Weinstein. She says three-quarters of her practice involves preventing charges from being filed. But singer D4vd’s murder case was impossible to keep quiet. Berk defended him against charges of killing 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez before withdrawing Aug. 31, when he qualified for a public defender — a growing trend in Hollywood (see Alan Jackson). Lisa Bloom Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Bloom Fudali Civil Litigation Two music cases, two different codas. Bloom’s firm settled Lauren Pisciotta’s harassment and assault suit against Kanye West in July, ending a two-year fight. But former Danity Kane singer Dawn Richard’s suit accusing Sean “Diddy” Combs of sexual assault and physical abuse was dismissed because most claims were filed too late. Bloom’s targets also include the FBI: Eight Jeffrey Epstein survivors she represents sued the bureau for allegedly failing to investigate reports of his abuse. Richard S. Busch Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Adams & Reese LLP Copyright Litigation After winning “Blurred Lines” for Marvin Gaye’s family, Busch is taking on artificial intelligence. In October, he sued Anthropic on behalf of Elvis Presley’s rights holders, including Authentic Brands Group, alleging its Claude models trained on 274 Presley songs without permission. The demand: up to $41.1 million — or about $150,000 per song. Anthropic disputes the claims. Similar suits for music publishers Reservoir Media and Round Hill have made Busch a recurring adversary for the AI company. Jeffrey Eisen Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Mitchell Silberberg & Knupp LLP Trusts & Estates Law More than 10 years after his death, Muhammad Ali is still one of Hollywood’s most active clients, and Eisen is the lawyer guarding his name. In January, the U.S. Postal Service issued an Ali Forever stamp, a milestone for an estate that the firm’s trusts and estates co-chair has helped steer through years of name-and-likeness deals. His firm’s other clients: Marilyn Monroe, Elvis Presley and Albert Einstein. Drew Findling Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text The Findling Law Firm Criminal Defense Litigation Findling and co-counsel Brian Steel dismantled the government’s murder-for-hire case against rapper Lil Durk, winning acquittals on all five counts. Findling argued that Durk’s former assistant, testifying for the prosecution, was himself the “mastermind,” urging jurors to see a “tsunami of reasonable doubt.” Afterward, 50 Cent dubbed him the “Billion Dollar Lawyer.” His client list also includes Cardi B and President Donald Trump. Bryan Freedman and Mitchell Schuster Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject (2) Logo text Liner Freedman; Meister Seelig & Schuster PLLC Civil & Commercial Litigation Freedman wielded the machete and Schuster the scalpel for actor-director Justin Baldoni in his battle with It Ends With U s co-star Blake Lively. His $400 million countersuit failed, but her harassment claims were dismissed, and the two sides settled without a payout. Lively later won $407,000 for defending against Baldoni’s defamation claim — just 5 percent of her $8 million legal-fee request, which Freedman called a “significant victory.” Thomas Giuffra Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Rheingold Giuffra Civil Litigation The lawyer for accusers of Harvey Weinstein and Sean “Diddy” Combs is now representing the woman at the center of the Cornell fraternity rape case. Giuffra’s suit alleges seven fraternity members drugged and gang-raped her and that Cornell failed her. As the case exploded online, his client faced threats, doxing and swatting, while supporters rallied under #IAmJaneDoe to protect her identity. New York Attorney General Letitia James is overseeing a criminal investigation. Shawn Holley and Kate Mangels Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Kinsella Holley Civil & Criminal Litigation An O.J. Simpson “Dream Team” alum, Holley represented pitcher Tyler Skaggs’ family in its wrongful death case against the Angels, arguing the team failed to stop an employee supplying players with drugs. The club settled during jury deliberations. Alongside Mangels, she also helped record label Del Records cut a proposed federal fine — for doing business with a sanctioned, cartel-linked concert promoter — from $6.7 million to $1.8 million. Restraining orders are also a specialty; the two have secured them for Cindy Crawford, Kaia Gerber and Lana Del Rey. Ambika Kumar Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Davis Wright Tremaine Technology & Media Litigation When gamers take their grievances to court, Kumar represents the companies behind the screens. She reps Microsoft and Mojang, creator of Minecraft , in suits accusing game companies of hooking children. Her clients also include Tinder and Hinge, for which she secured dismissals in two cases alleging the apps failed to remove user profiles and messages. She also helped technology trade group NetChoice keep key provisions of California’s age-appropriate online design law blocked on appeal. Alan Jackson (and the L.A. County Public Defender’s Office) Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Werksman Jackson Criminal Defense Litigation Jackson, who has defended Harvey Weinstein and Kevin Spacey, exited as Nick Reiner’s attorney in January. That notorious patricide-and-matricide case is now being handled by what’s rapidly turning into Hollywood’s hottest new legal shop — the L.A. County Public Defender’s Office. Not only is public defender Kimberly Greene now representing Reiner, but her colleagues Walid Kandeel and Lisa Roth took over singer D4vd’s murder defense from Blair Berk in August. Jackson, meanwhile, is teaming with former client Karen Read for a true-crime podcast, Read Between the Lines , debuting in early 2027. Sarah Moses and Esra Hudson Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject (3) Logo text Manatt, Phelps & Phillips LLP Civil Litigation Hudson and Moses didn’t just get Justin Baldoni’s $400 million countersuit against Blake Lively and Ryan Reynolds thrown out; they helped stick him with $407,000 of Lively’s legal bill, securing the first federal court award under California’s law protecting sexual harassment accusers from retaliatory defamation suits. Moses helped draft the motion; Hudson led Lively’s team. Lively’s own claims ended in a settlement without a payout. Luke Nikas and Alex Spiro Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject (2) Logo text Quinn Emanuel Criminal & Civil Litigation Nikas won $102.2 million for the Morgan Art Foundation against publisher Michael McKenzie over unauthorized and altered works based on Robert Indiana’s LOVE — the familiar sculpture with the tilted O. He calls it the largest art-litigation verdict on record. His partner Spiro had more mixed results with client Elon Musk: Delaware’s Supreme Court reinstated his roughly $56 billion Tesla pay package, but a San Francisco jury found he misled Twitter investors. Deanna Paul and Mark Geragos Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject; Gotpap/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images/Getty Images Logo text Geragos & Geragos APC Criminal Defense Litigation Some brothers fared better than others. Paul defended celebrity realtor Tal Alexander against charges that he and his siblings drugged and sexually trafficked women. The jury convicted all three, and each received a 30-year sentence. Geragos had more luck with the Lyle and Erik Menendez, helping them secure a new parole hearing roughly 17 months ahead of schedule after the brothers were denied release last year. His TMZ appearances stirred up some controversy, though, with Geragos’ comments on the Cornell fraternity rape case prompted the accuser’s lawyer to allege that he was effectively assisting the defense team, which includes his daughter, Teny, at Agnifilo Intrater. Geragos denies it. Kevin Reddington Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Kevin Reddington Law Office Criminal Defense Litigation He doesn’t represent Hollywood actors or battle for studios, but the 75-year-old Massachusetts attorney did become one of 2026’s biggest reality stars. His livestreamed defense of Lindsay Clancy, accused of killing her three children, inspired more than 16,500 TikTok videos under his hashtag, autograph requests outside court and fan-made “Better Call Kevin” merch. Reddington argued Clancy was not criminally responsible due to postpartum psychosis. The jury deadlocked in September. Mathew Rosengart Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Greenberg Traurig LLP Media & Entertainment Litigation After helping Britney Spears escape her conservatorship, Rosengart fought for FKA twigs to reclaim her voice, winning an agreement lifting restrictions on discussing her sexual abuse allegations against ex-boyfriend Shia LaBeouf. He’s also defending Selena Gomez against investors who accuse her of failing to deliver on commitments to build and promote her mental health startup, Wondermind. Kristina Royce Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Blank Rome LLP Matrimonial & Family Law Royce has handled splits for Arnold Schwarzenegger, Channing Tatum and Forest Whitaker. Now she’s representing Lori Loughlin, whose marriage to Mossimo Giannulli survived the college admissions scandal and prison terms for both but ended in separation after nearly 28 years of marriage, with Loughlin filing for divorce in September. Martin “Marty” Singer Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Singer Weinsten Entertainment & Business Litigation A letter from Marty Singer has ruined many a Hollywood morning. In November, he accused filmmaker Yi Zhou of harassing Jeremy Renner after she alleged the actor sent explicit messages and threatened to call ICE. He also represented Priscilla Presley against former business partners who accused her of concealing a $25 million jewelry collection; they dropped that suit in February, retaining the right to refile. In March, Lavely & Singer became Singer Weinsten Wolf & Jonelis, adding three longtime partners to the firm’s name. Brian Steel Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text The Steel Law Firm, P.C. Criminal Defense Litigation Most lawyers hope for a referral. Steel got a Drake song named after him. After representing Young Thug and joining Sean “Diddy” Combs’ defense, the Atlanta attorney teamed with Drew Findling to win Lil Durk acquittals on all five counts in his federal murder-for-hire trial. Fans swarmed him outside court after the verdict. Durk remains jailed ahead of a separate racketeering trial in August 2027. Robert Strauss and Jonathan Forster Logo text Weinstock Manion Trusts & Estates Law Strauss and Forster help Hollywood’s wealthy pass fortunes to the next generation, minimizing estate taxes and planning for the transfer of family businesses. Lately, some clients have acquired another adviser: a chatbot. Strauss told CNBC that clients are uploading trust documents to AI, then returning with suggested revisions that can take hours to review. “I have not actually received a single workable suggestion from that process,” he says. The firm is updating its contracts to warn that sharing confidential documents with AI “lawyers” could jeopardize attorney-client privilege. Adam Streisand Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Sheppard Trusts & Estates Law After helping secure Lachlan Murdoch’s control of Fox and News Corp, Streisand moved to another family power struggle: Jeanie Buss versus her five siblings over whether to sell the family’s remaining 17.8 percent Lakers stake. Her brothers and sister want to cash out alongside billionaire Mark Walter, who bought control of the team in 2025 and has agreed to sell to Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner at a $12.5 billion valuation. Buss wants to retain the shares. A hearing is set for Dec. 8. Laura Wasser Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Wasser Cooperman & Mandles Family Law Wasser doesn’t just handle divorces; she models for them, fronting fashion label Reformation’s “Divorce Collection” campaign this year. For Sia, she filed an October settlement keeping the singer the primary custodial parent of her toddler with Dan Bernad, who receives $42,500 a month in child support. Her newest client is Hila Klein, who filed to divorce husband and H3 Podcast co-host Ethan Klein on Nov. 2 after publicly accusing him of an affair. Douglas Wigdor Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Wigdor LLP Employment Law Wigdor is leaving no stone unturned in Julia Ormond’s ongoing sexual assault suit against Harvey Weinstein — pursuing Disney, Miramax and CAA for allegedly failing to protect her. His firm even won an order requiring former CAA chairman Michael Ovitz to answer questions under oath about the agency’s representation of the actress. Other clients include Cassie Ventura, whose rape and sex trafficking suit against Sean “Diddy” Combs settled a day after filing. The firm is also suing Leon Black, alleging the financier filed retaliatory lawsuits to intimidate lawyers representing his sexual assault accusers. Laura Zwicker Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Logo text Greenberg Glusker Trusts & Estates For Zwicker’s wealthy clients, moving away can be as complicated as passing a fortune down. Alongside estate planning for entertainers and multinational families, she advises on the tax consequences of changing countries. California, for one, doesn’t surrender its taxpayers easily. She told The San Francisco Standard that auditors examine ATM withdrawals and Apple Pay transactions to determine whether residents have really left — or just their tax bills. “They want to see all of the data on all of your devices,” she says. This story appeared in the Nov. 18 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine.

title: Golden Globes Category Chaos: When ‘The Drama’ Is a Comedy…
full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Feinberg Plus Icon Scott Feinberg Executive Editor of Awards ScottFeinberg Follow Sign Up View All November 20, 2026 9:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Illustrated by Christopher Hughes The Drama is a comedy — or so say the backers of the film, about an engaged couple’s darkest secrets, in their submission for the Golden Globes , which requires all films be entered as either A) a drama or B) a musical or a comedy. And that’s not even one of this year’s more questionable submissions. Other comedy entries include I Play Rocky , about the making of Rocky (which competed at the Globes as a drama); Obsession , about a young woman’s loss of agency; Tender Loving Care , about the frustrations of two young women, including the decline of one’s father; Artificial , about AI growing out of control; and Project Hail Mary , about a man sent into space against his will to try to stave off the end of the world. Meanwhile, Club Kid , about a man-child who ends up with a child — widely described as an elevated version of Adam Sandler’s comedy Big Daddy — has been entered as a drama. Related Stories Movies IDFA: 'The Year of the Ghost' and 'Memories of Lightning' Win Amsterdam Doc Fest Awards TV CBS Inks New Deal to Air Kennedy Center Honors Yes, all of the aforementioned musical/comedy submissions have moments of laughter and all of the dramas have elements of drama — but still, these classifications are pretty eyebrow-raising, begging the questions: What is going on? And is there a better way? *** The first Globes were held in 1944. There were no genre-specific Globes categories until the eighth, when the lead acting categories were split into two, one for dramas, the other for musicals/comedies. The following year, the same split was implemented for best picture. That category was reunified for the 11th ceremony, but the split was brought back for the 12th and every year since, helping to attract more stars to the ceremony. Until 2023, Globes category submissions were made by studios and reviewed by the HFPA’s reminders list committee, which rarely overturned anything, even as dramas with music passed as musicals ( Ray , Walk the Line and Rocketman ), dramas with few laughs passed as comedies ( Ghost , The Tourist and My Week With Marilyn ) and comedies passed as dramas ( All About Eve , Born Yesterday , Harvey and Sunset Boulevard — all in the same year). Once in a blue moon, the committee would reject a submission ( Promising Young Woman as a musical/comedy), but it usually deferred to studios’ preferences. Frustrations burst into the open in 2015 after The Martian , a film about an astronaut stranded on Mars, was submitted and accepted as a musical/comedy. Judd Apatow, whose comedy Trainwreck was in contention that year, tweeted, “Trying to dominate the comedy category when you are really a drama afraid of dramatic competition is a punk move.” The Martian ended up beating Trainwreck for best picture, something Apatow was still smarting over when he presented at this year’s Globes: “My film Trainwreck lost best comedy to Ridley Scott’s The Martian . You know Ridley Scott, America’s favorite comedy director — director of such hilarious comedies as Gladiator , Blade Runner and Alien ? I can’t wait till later tonight when best comedy is won by Hamnet .” But ownership of the Globes had changed in 2023 (the Globes now share the same owners as THR ), resulting in widespread reforms. This year’s rules declare: “Motion pictures shall be entered in the category that best matches the overall intent, tone and content of the film. Therefore, a motion picture that is primarily intended to have a serious or dramatic tone but contains comedic overtones or elements shall be entered as a drama as opposed to a comedy. Likewise, a motion picture that is primarily intended to have a comedic or satirical tone but contains dramatic overtones or elements shall be entered as a comedy as opposed to a drama.” Once the film submission period ends (Nov. 24 this year), an eligibility committee comprising current Globes voters (the quantity and names are kept private) evaluates every submission for “potential misclassification issues.” If found, they “may contact the studio … to discuss those issues and to resolve them informally.” Eventually, the eligibility committee meets with a review committee to discuss any outstanding concerns, and those committees — or at least members of them who have seen a film in question — vote to determine if a change is necessary; two-thirds must favor a change for one to occur. *** The Drama , starring Robert Pattinson and Zendaya, was submitted in the musical/comedy category for this year’s Golden Globes. Courtesy of A24 Why do people try to game the Globes categories? Because the nationally telecast Globes ceremony provides the biggest spotlight for awards contenders before Oscar nominations voting (the 2027 Globes will take place Jan. 10, and Oscar nomination voting starts the next morning), making it highly valuable for a film or individual to be represented at the ceremony as a nominee or, better still, a winner. There usually are fewer standout musicals and comedies than dramas, meaning it’s often easier to land a nom or win if a drama can pass as a musical/comedy. (This year’s aforementioned musical/comedy submissions surely wanted to get out of the way of The Odyssey .) Another motivation: Studios with multiple films prefer to not have them pitted against one another. (A24 probably wants Club Kid to compete as a drama because it already has The Invite and The Debut up for best musical/comedy, just as Neon probably wants Artificial to compete as a comedy because it already has All of a Sudden , Fjord and Paper Tiger up for best drama.) It remains to be seen whether the Globes’ eligibility committee will overturn some of this year’s submissions. (Reports suggest it already rejected Michael as a musical/comedy.) Moving forward, it would make everyone’s life easier if the Globes consolidated its genre-specific categories — picture, actor and actress — into single categories with 12 slots rather than divided categories with six each. Or, if the Globes prefers to continue to have multiple categories for each in order to yield twice as many winners, it might consider retaining the “drama” label for one but changing the other to “genre,” which would better describe recent musical/comedy nominees like Poor Things , The Substance and Bugonia . title: Peak Halftime Show: The A-List Machine Eventizing Pro Games
full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin , Ethan Millman November 20, 2026 8:56am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images Nearly 73,000 fans inside Rio De Janeiro’s Maracanã Stadium rocked out to Ricky Martin and Brazilian DJ Pedro Sampaio on Sept. 27, when the duo performed their song “pikito pikito” live for the first time. But they weren’t headlining a concert — they were playing a halftime show. The NFL has long held global ambitions, but this is the year it leaned into music to serve as a sort of cultural diplomacy. The Rio game, between the Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys, may be the best example, combining a global superstar in Martin with a local talent. “There was a lot of preparation and many hours of rehearsals leading up to the performance,” Martin tells The Hollywood Reporter , “but it was one of those experiences where everything came together beautifully.” He adds, “These are memories I’ll carry with me for a long time.” Puerto Rican singer Ricky Martin performs during halftime of the game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Dallas Cowboys at Maracana Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Buda Mendes/Getty Images In fact, the NFL has seven halftime shows planned this season, kicking off with the Jonas Brothers in Melbourne on Sept. 10, running through The Warning in Mexico City on Nov. 22. It’s also part of a concerted effort to elevate games into cultural events. Just look at Nov. 25, when U2 will perform during a halftime show for Netflix’s Thanksgiving Eve game at SoFi Stadium between the L.A. Rams and Green Bay Packers. “There’s really this gathering momentum about how we can further eventize some of the parts on our schedule and our calendar,” Hans Schroeder, executive vp and chief media officer of the NFL, told reporters in October. The league is leaning into halftime shows as the sports world overall has been more heavily embracing music programming in games. FIFA for instance, had its first World Cup Final halftime show this summer, with Coldplay’s Chris Martin curating a lineup that included BTS, Madonna and Justin Bieber. The NCAA, meanwhile, tapped EDM act The Chainsmokers to play a “bridge show” between the two Final Four games. The NHL has dug in, too, tapping Benson Boone to headline the first intermission during this year’s Winter Classic on New Year’s Eve. Madonna performs alongside Ronaldinho and Ronaldo during the FIFA World Cup 2026 final match between Spain and Argentina at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19, 2026. Catherine Ivill – AMA/Getty Images “The NFL and all these leagues understand that to grow the game internationally and even domestically for the younger generation, they need to find organic ways to get those eyeballs,” says Tyler Stimmel, a booking agent in UTA’s music brand partnerships division. He handled booking on many of the NFL’s international events this year, including Jonas Brothers, Burna Boy in Paris, The Warning and Drew Baldridge in Munich. “It all stems from the younger generation,” Stimmel says, pointing toward a recent USC Annenberg study that suggested nearly 80 percent of Gen Z respondents in a survey suggested they’d go to a sporting event because of concerts and other brand activations rather than because of the game itself. It’s beneficial to the talent, too, with international acts getting a shot to play before a wide swath of stateside NFL fans who otherwise likely wouldn’t have been exposed to their music. The agent adds, “We live in a highly saturated pop culture ecosystem the NFL wants more ways to cut through. “Music is the most natural way because we already know where to put the show, and you can pick a booking to tap into a version of culture that people within the region can easily relate to.” In the U.S., that means working with such partners as Netflix to create more event-sized moments, like having U2 perform. “Netflix has leaned in because they see the success of Super Bowl and the Super Bowl halftime show, and it draws more eyes and it brings more attention and it brings more people, and not necessarily all avid football fans,” says Jon Barker, senior VP of global event production and operations for the NFL. “Now we’re tapping into casual fans, now we’re tapping into new fans, and it’s just one more element that opens another door for somebody to walk into the ecosystem of football and participate.” Unlike the Super Bowl, which is booked by Jay-Z’s Roc Nation (next year’s headliner is Jay-Z himself), the league books its other halftime shows itself, though Barker notes that there is close coordination with its media rights partners. “It gets a little complicated, to be honest with you, in trying to find the right balance,” Barker says of the booking process. “Who is touring and is available? Who can put on a show that can fill a stadium? Who will translate well and do well on television? Who is the right act for the audience that’s inside this area, and who is the right act that will attract new fans that will be interested in what we’re doing?” Burna Boy performs on stage during the halftime show at the NFL game between Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints at Stade de France on October 25, 2026 in Paris, France. Catherine Steenkeste/Getty Images Stimmel, for his part, describes the process as sophisticated, saying the NFL has heavily relied on its regional offices throughout the world, identifying artists who are a major draw in each market but who can pull viewers from several verticals. “Burna Boy in Paris in particular is one that checks off a lot of those boxes,” he says. “He was one of the first Nigerian artists to sell out Stade de France, so we know he is popular there, but he can draw from Africa, North America.” While the increased bookings may bring in more younger viewers, they may not always be a popular offering to older fans, who might prefer to see just a traditional halftime report with pundits rather than a concert. Stimmel acknowledges that critique but adds that “they want this to appeal to everyone, but the leagues are recognizing that in order to sustain the sport, it has to appeal to younger fans.” NFL exec Barker says the league isn’t done expanding its halftime ambitions, noting that while “there’s probably a limit and the right balance, I don’t think we’re there yet,” even if it maintains the Super Bowl as the ultimate showcase. From the league’s point of view, the performances are ultimately about growing the game — and reasserting the league as the most culturally relevant piece of American pop culture. “The way that we think about music is the same way we think about art, the same way we think about fashion,” says Barker, adding that the more ways “we can open to bring somebody in and show them the sport, the better off we all are.” Halftime show past and future: U2 played the Super Bowl in 2002. The band is booked for a Nov. 25 NFL game, when U2 will perform during a halftime show for Netflix’s Thanksgiving Eve game at SoFi Stadium. title: ‘Bouchra’ Filmmakers Orian Barki and Meriem Bennani on Crafting the 3D-Animated, Autofiction Film: ‘Through Specificity, You Can Reach Truth’
full_text: Nov 20, 2026 8:30am PT ‘Bouchra’ Filmmakers Orian Barki and Meriem Bennani on Crafting the 3D-Animated, Autofiction Film: ‘Through Specificity, You Can Reach Truth’ By Angelique Jackson Plus Icon Angelique Jackson angelique814 Latest ‘Madden’: Why Christian Bale Ranks Raiders Owner Al Davis as One of His Favorite Characters and the Jewelry He Took Home From Set 19 hours ago Netflix and Disney Alum Tendo Nagenda Joins Proximity Media as President 21 hours ago Poorna Jagannathan, Clark Gregg, Isabela Ferrer, Christopher Rodriguez Marquette and Paul Ben-Victor Join ‘Twenty-Seven’ (EXCLUSIVE) 23 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Meriem Bennani never set out to make a movie quite as personal as “ Bouchra .” “I’m a pretty private person — hard to believe, probably, after seeing this film,” Bennani joked, sitting with her co-director Orian Barki for a Variety’s Screening Series Q&A. Sure, the animated film was always a work of autofiction: “Bouchra” explores the journey of a 35-year-old Moroccan lesbian navigating life and love in New York City and writing the script for an autobiographical film. (Bouchra, the title character, is a jackal and all the cast are anthropomorphic animals, mirroring the duo’s first project, the 2020 web series “2 Lizards.”) The movie was also inspired by Bennani’s mother’s reaction to her coming out as queer. But the movie wasn’t supposed to be about their relationship. So how did it end up that way? Related Stories Jennifer Lopez Wears 186-Carat Diamond Necklace to 'JLo Show' Premiere: 'There's Security All Around' Jennifer Lopez on the ‘JLo Show’ Concert Film, Her ‘Happy Era’ and Moving on From Divorce: 'What I Thought Love Was Really Isn’t Love’ Bennani and Barki had begun developing the project with their collaborators, cinematographer John Michael Boling and head of animation Jason Coombs, but something wasn’t quite clicking. “We had the script, but as we were editing the dialogues and starting to put the storyboards [together], we felt like there was something we were still looking for, and it’s the heart of the film,” Bennani recalled. So, she told Barki she needed to call her mom to get more insight into her perspective. Why did she react that way when Bennani came out? The call was purely for research, but Bennani knew it’d be prudent to record the conversation. “Bouchra” Courtesy of 2 Lizards Productions “I knew I would be too emotional to be there as a director. I would be there as a daughter,” she explained. “So I recorded them and then I played them for Orian. … And we knew in that moment, that was the film and that we needed to put these conversations in the film.” Those recordings became the new framework for the movie as the filmmakers lasered in on this personal narrative over a more synthesized version of a Moroccan lesbian’s experience. “Through specificity, you can reach truth,” Bennani said. “And when I say truth, I don’t mean realism. Just an emotional truth.” The experimental indie film debuted as part of Bennani’s art exhibition at Fondazione Prada in Milan (which backed the film), then was part of the official selection at TIFF in 2025. The feature has picked up a handful of prizes as it traveled the art house and film festival circuits, including the Gold Q-Hugo prize at the Chicago International Film Festival. (“Bouchra” is now streaming on Mubi.) “People are really into seeing a film that is original and looks different and is so handcrafted,” Barki said, reflecting on the positive response. “I was happy to see that people are just down for a new story and a new visual.” One of the most poignant pieces of feedback came from a friend who told Barki, “I always thought that my parents loving me means that they have to understand everything about me. And maturing, I learned that I can receive their love without them having to actually understand every detail of my existence the same way that I understand it.” Without necessarily intending to, Barki’s friend had zeroed in on a central theme of the meta movie. “The movie is about a mother-daughter relationship that has this foundation of love, [which] is what gets them to have all these conversations,” Barki explained. “And in a way, it doesn’t matter if they’ll understand everything about it, but just the willingness to have this conversation is already the acceptance and the love.” Watch the video above to learn more about Bennani and Barki’s artistry; how they drew inspiration from Wong Kar-wai’s “Chungking Express” and Martin Scorsese’s “After Hours”; and what Bennani’s mother made of the finished film. Meriem Bennani and Orian Barki speak onstage with Variety’s Angelique Jackson at the PMC Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles. title: Mckenna Grace on Her ‘Hunger Games’ Press Tour Looks for ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’: Maysilee’s Style Is Her ‘Form of Defiance Against the Capitol’
full_text: Getty Images for Lionsgate Mckenna Grace has been on a red carpet run for the ages during the global press tour for “The Hunger Games : Sunrise on the Reaping.” Over the last few weeks, the 20-year-old actress (and certified “Hunger Games” fangirl) has donned nearly two dozen looks that referenced the original trilogy or franchise star Jennifer Lawrence. Grace, who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner (and her twin sister, Merilee), launched the tour with an archival Monique Lhuillier gown that evoked Lawrence’s wedding dress as Katniss in “Catching Fire.” Then, for the film’s final premiere on Monday night in New York City, Grace glided onto the red carpet in a cobalt blue Pamella Roland gown — with feathered wings! — mirroring the iconic Mockingjay look that bridal gown turned into. Related Stories Veteran Publicist Bill Harrison and Creative Director Johnny Wujek Join Nonprofit Art of Elysium (EXCLUSIVE) Gemma Chan Says She’d ‘Absolutely’ Play a Bond Girl Amid Fan-Casting: ‘I’m Flattered’ Like Katniss, Grace’s Maysilee aims to defy the Capitol — something the actress wanted to portray in real life, too. “Maysilee’s form of rebellion was also her style and holding onto her personality in the face of the Capitol,” Grace told Variety’s Antonio Ferme at the New York City premiere. “I felt like I’d be doing myself a disservice not paying homage to all of the incredible performers and costume designers from the previous films.” Grace joined Variety for a longer chat a few days earlier, checking in on Zoom the morning after the Los Angeles fan event for “Sunrise on the Reaping,” where she recreated another of Katniss’ dresses from “Catching Fire.” With just two stops left on the press tour (Mexico and New York City), Grace is in between fittings for her final two outfits, both of which paid homage to the mockingjay that started it all. After all, her character is the original owner of the mockingjay pin. Joseph Zada (as Haymitch) and Mckenna Grace (as Maysilee) in “ The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping .” Murray Close/Lionsgate Her character, Maysilee, is the hot-headed, dignified ally of Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada), who similarly wishes to take down the Capitol and stop the Hunger Games. Although District 12 is known as the poorest district, she prides herself in her fine dresses and overzealous amounts of jewelry — something she continues to prioritize after being reaped. “I didn’t want it to be like, ‘Oh, I’m an actor and I’m in the Hunger Games, but I still want my character to look pretty and have good, snatched makeup,’” she says. “To me, her fashion and her style isn’t a vain thing. It’s her form of defiance against the Capitol.” Below, Grace talks to Variety about playing Maysilee, details she included from Suzanne Collins’ novel and fangirling over franchise stars Jennifer Lawrence and Sam Claflin. You famously fought for the braid in your hair that Maysilee wore in the fan film about the 50th “Hunger Games.” Are there any other details that you fought to have included in this movie? There’s a lot. I got the braid and the bangs [from the fan film]. I know this is silly and it’s not something that’s mentioned in the books, but I wanted Maysilee to have different colored eyeshadows in all the scenes that we see her in. That’s how she stood out as a twin and in District 12: all of her necklaces, dresses, jewelry and her braid. The Capitol is appointing them clothes. She can’t have her personality shine through with her fashion, which is something she really enjoys. She has this line where she’s like, “Do we all have to look like triplets?” because they put them in all the same clothes, and they’re bland. Throughout that, she’s still finding ways to stand out and be seen as a classy person. And a person, not an animal. Somebody with fashion. Somebody with personality, with dignity. So I wanted her to have that little defiance with her eyeshadow. Mckenna Grace as Maysilee in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.” Murray Close/Lionsgate I also made sure that she wore a bunch of rings and jewelry. I made sure that her sleeves were torn off whenever we see her in the games, which is random. But in the books, it’s mentioned that whenever they see her again, she’s missing her sleeves because she ripped them off, and she has burns up her shoulders. Also, something important to me was when Haymitch and Maysilee sit down for their picnic, I got Jo [Zada] to add back in — because this was not in the original scene — where he tells Maysilee about how his mom had twin girls that didn’t make it. I told Jo and Francis [Lawrence, the film’s director] that I felt that was so important because Maysilee, for the first time, is giving Haymitch some vulnerability. And he gives that back to her. That’s so important for their relationship and such a beautiful thing for her to hear at that time. I had a lot of things that I wanted to get in there! O ne scene that I wish we had from the book is when Maysilee is talking about how she doesn’t want to be a twin and work behind that candy counter for the rest of her life. Have you ever thought about what she would be doing with her life if she wasn’t chosen for the games? I don’t know, because I don’t think that there’s any version — I mean, of course there are ways that she’s found joy, even within the games when Haymitch brings out the juice, and they sit and have their picnic. That’s a moment of joy; that doesn’t come with worrying about all the heaviness of the world in the games. And there are moments of connection and joy throughout it, but she’s a very angry character. I don’t know if there is a version of Maysilee, even not being chosen by the games, where she feels truly happy in the world that she lives in or the circumstances that she was born into. She didn’t set up that system or the world that she’s in, and I don’t think that she was ever truly happy in District 12, because she was just so angry at the way that it was all designed and at the games just for existing. A scene from “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.” Murray Close/Lionsgate How did you find the balance between Maysilee’s anger and her big heart in moments like when she’s braiding Ampert’s (Percy Daggs IV) token? It was really fun. She is learning to be more outwardly kind and a little bit more sensitive to the others around her, and she’s learning how to be a sister and a healer and a friend more than just being angry and lashing out at everybody throughout the film. That’s kind of what her arc is. But I didn’t want that arc of her learning to be kinder to diminish her anger. I didn’t want it to be like, “Oh, this angry female character all of a sudden learns how to be a sister and a mother and a friend, and she’s not angry anymore and has found happiness in that.” While she finds happiness in being kind to the people around her and protecting them, she’s still a very angry character. It’s really important to show young women, and anyone in general, that the two can coexist. You can be very angry at the world. You can be very loud in standing up for yourself and standing up for the people around you, but you can also be kind throughout that. That’s something we lose a lot; that it has to be one or the other. But no, you can stand up; you can speak out. You don’t have to box up your emotions and the things that you believe in, or make yourself more digestible for the people around you. You can still have your personality. You can still be loud about the things that you believe in, but you can still be kind and have conversations and care about people and stick up for the people around you throughout that. As a “Hunger Games” fan, how crazy is it to see that Jennifer Lawrence and Sam Claflin are commenting on videos of you guys? It is ridiculous! It’s insane. Jennifer Lawrence’s comment was so funny. And the fact that Sam Claflin is commenting on my video of me dressed up [with] Finnick’s abs painted on my shirt — that was the funniest thing. I will never not be exposed to any celebrity that I am the biggest fan of. Between him and Josh [Hutcherson] and Jen, it’s just ridiculous. It’s so surreal. We’re all such huge fans of them. Jo and I spent so many nights mulling over Josh and Jen, and I spent so long studying Sam for Finnick. It’s such an honor that they even know who I am. Richardson runs Ivy Lion with wife Zaire-Julion Richardson and the duo has secured private investment as part of an ongoing seven-figure capital raise to support its expansion into film and TV. The funding will go towards acquiring and optioning book IP and plays for screen adaptions, as well as developing and packaging projects for production. On the TV front, the company has a slate of scripted projects in active development with talent attached. The feature slate is also growing with IP acquisitions seen as a central priority. title: ‘Ramayana’ Star Sai Pallavi, Ravi Kishan’s ‘Spider-Man’ Anecdote, Grammy Winner Ricky Kej Light Up International Film Festival of India Opening in Goa
full_text: × Nov 20, 2026 8:07am PT ‘Ramayana’ Star Sai Pallavi, Ravi Kishan’s ‘Spider-Man’ Anecdote, Grammy Winner Ricky Kej Light Up International Film Festival of India Opening in Goa By Udita Jhunjhunwala , Naman Ramachandran Add us as a Google Preferred Source Naman Ramachandran The 57th International Film Festival of India opened in Goa on Friday, with “Lagaan” director Ashutosh Gowariker setting out a “Stories Without Borders” program in his first year as festival director and Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant renewing his push for a film city in the state. Paweł Pawlikowski’s “Fatherland,” which shared the best director prize at Cannes this year, opened the festival. The ceremony at the Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Indoor Stadium began with the national anthem “Jana Gana Mana” and national song “Vande Mataram,” followed by a ceremonial lamp lighting with Sawant, National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) chair G. Krishna Kumar, Gowariker and several other dignitaries. Related Stories Gemma Chan Says She’d ‘Absolutely’ Play a Bond Girl Amid Fan-Casting: ‘I’m Flattered’ BMG’s Concord Originals Preps Supernatural Gothic Horror Pic ‘Wolf at the Door’ (EXCLUSIVE) Bollywood star Kartik Aaryan was in attendance, along with Sai Pallavi , who plays Sita in Nitesh Tiwari’s blockbuster “ Ramayana .” Jury chairs Aanand L. Rai (“Tanu Weds Manu”), who heads the international jury, and filmmakers Madhur Bhandarkar and Himanshu Sekhar Khatua, who led the Indian Panorama feature and non-feature juries respectively, were also in the audience. The festival runs through Nov. 28. Three-time Grammy winner Ricky Kej set the tone with “A World of Cinema Through Music,” an orchestral performance built around a medley of film themes played with Indian instruments. It moved from “The Godfather,” “Parasite” and “Rashomon” to “The Lord of the Rings,” Satyajit Ray’s “Pather Panchali,” “Doctor Zhivago,” “The Good, the Bad and the Ugly,” “La Bamba,” Gowariker’s own “Lagaan” and “Mission: Impossible 2.” Kej returned later with a set mixing musical traditions from Italy, Mongolia, the U.S., India and the U.A.E. A peacock dance, symbolizing the festival’s Golden Peacock award, also featured on the program. Goa has been IFFI’s permanent home since 2004, and its streets and landmarks have turned up in films such as “Dil Chahta Hai” and “Dear Zindagi.” “But our ambition goes further,” Sawant said. “We want Goa to become the place where the films are produced and completed.” The state’s plans include a proposed film city with facilities for pre-production, post-production, VFX and film education, which Sawant said would encourage local filmmaking, draw filmmakers from across India and open new avenues for young Goan creative professionals. He has raised the idea at earlier editions of the festival, seeking central government support for a Goa film city at the 2021 opening ceremony. Sawant also pointed to the Goa Regulation of Film Shooting Act 2021 and an online single-window permit system run by the Entertainment Society of Goa, and said the state’s film financing scheme for Goan producers is being revised to cover newer formats and digital productions. With virtual production, AI, animation and VFX changing how films are made, he said Goa wants a stake in that next phase. Gowariker, the Oscar-nominated director of “Lagaan,” “Swades” and “Jodhaa Akbar,” took the job in May. He told the audience that until now he had only experienced festivals as a filmmaker who flies in with a film, does a Q&A and leaves, and that his team shaped this edition by asking what stories actually do for people. “We live in a time when we are more connected than ever, and yet it has also become very easy to stay inside our own circle,” Gowariker said. “Borders today are not only lines on a map. They’re also habits. A story is one of the few things that can cross such a line without a passport.” The international program comprises 159 films from 86 countries, picked from more than 1,400 submissions, according to Gowariker, alongside 76 Indian films in 18 languages. Romanian director Alina Șerban’s “I Matter,” a Romania-Germany-Belgium production, is the mid-festival film, and Singaporean director Anthony Chen’s “We Are All Strangers” closes the event. Spain is this year’s Country of Honor and Russia the Partner Country. A showcase of 21 films from BRICS nations, a first for the festival, opens with “Ramayana” on Nov. 22. Fifteen films compete for five awards in the International Competition. Prize money across the festival’s jury awards totals INR1.36 crore ($147,000), including INR51 lakh ($55,000) and the Golden Peacock for best film. Rai’s jury also includes Romanian director Bogdan Mureșanu, Venezuelan sound designer María Alejandra Rojas, Thai director Ratchapoom Boonbunchachoke and Argentine director Sol Berruezo Pichon-Rivière. Eighteen titles in the lineup are their countries’ Oscar submissions. The program also counts nine world premieres, two international premieres, 24 Asian premieres and 116 India premieres. The Indian Panorama section brings 25 features and 20 non-features from across the country, chosen by Bhandarkar’s and Khatua’s juries. It opens with Aditya Dhar’s Hindi-language “Dhurandhar” and Leena Yadav’s “Becoming,” a film in Ladakhi. A curated package of 15 Goan films and six award winners from the 19th Mumbai International Film Festival complete the Indian slate. Gowariker also spoke about the WAVES Film Bazaar, the festival’s market, where buyers, programmers and producers from Paris, Busan and London mix with filmmakers such as a young director from Guwahati in northeastern India who had ridden a train for two days to get there. “Sometimes a great deal of cinema begins with someone saying, ‘Come, let’s have a coffee,’ and the other person saying, ‘Sure, I have ten minutes,'” he said. “Three hours later, there’s a co-production.” On the heritage front, the festival marks the centenary of Polish director Andrzej Wajda and revisits the work of Prem Nazir, Suryakant Mandhare, Raj Kumar, Uttam Kumar, Shakti Samanta, composers O.P. Nayyar and Ravi across Hindi, Bengali, Marathi and Malayalam cinema. “Lagaan” celebrates its 25th anniversary at the festival. Two new sections, Animation and Films About Films, feature Brad Bird’s “Ray Gunn” and Barnaby Thompson’s documentary “Maverick: The Epic Adventures of David Lean.” Women directed 52 films in the international lineup and first-time filmmakers 62. Of the 21 titles across the festival’s three competitions, 10 are by women and 12 are debuts. Chanchal Kumar, secretary of India’s Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, said, “A border may define where a story begins, it need not define how far that story can travel.” Chief guest Ravi Kishan, a Bhojpuri star and second-term Member of Parliament from Gorakhpur, looked back on a 34-year career spanning almost 700 films in Hindi, Bhojpuri, Telugu, Kannada, Tamil, Gujarati and Marathi, including Kiran Rao’s “Laapataa Ladies,” India’s Oscar entry. “Many years ago, I had the chance to lend my voice to Spider-Man as Tobey Maguire, and what, in Bhojpuri!” Kishan said. “Imagine there was no border and it was a blockbuster in Bihar.” Gowariker urged the audience to spend part of the nine days on a film they would not normally pick. “Watch at least one film in a language you do not understand, a film from a country you have not visited, and by a filmmaker whose name you have not heard,” he said. “Let the subtitles do their work. title: Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Makes $21 Million in Previews
full_text: × Nov 20, 2026 8:05am PT Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Makes $21 Million in Previews By Jordan Moreau Plus Icon Jordan Moreau Latest Box Office: ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Makes $21 Million in Previews 2 hours ago How ‘Hunger Games’ Stars Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson Return for ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ 17 hours ago ‘The Nightingale’ Trailer: Dakota and Elle Fanning Share the Screen for the First Time and Play Sisters During WWII in Adaptation of Popular Book 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source ©Lions Gate/Courtesy Everett Collection It’s time to head back to Panem with “ The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping ” this weekend. The latest entry in the Lionsgate series has made $21 million in Thursday previews and early screenings Wednesday at the box office. It’s expected to open with more than $100 million at the box office, though the studio is more cautiously predicting an $85 million debut. However, some estimates put the sixth “Hunger Games” movie even higher at $125 million due to the franchise’s fandom and the return of some fan-favorite characters. Related Stories ‘La Bola Negra’ to Receive International Star Award at Palm Springs International Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE) Jennifer Lopez Wears 186-Carat Diamond Necklace to 'JLo Show' Premiere: 'There's Security All Around' If the opening crosses $100 million, it’ll be one of five movies this year to surpass the milestone and join “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” ($360 million), “Toy Story 5” ($159 million), “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” ($131 million) and “The Odyssey” ($123 million). “Sunrise on the Reaping” comes three years after the last “Hunger Games” prequel, “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.” The 2023 movie made $5.75 million in previews and opened to $44 million. It ended its run with $363 million globally, making it a success against its $100 million budget. “Sunrise on the Reaping” should open closer to the original 2010s franchise starring Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson, which will help as it carries a $150 million budget. The first “Hunger Games” debuted to $152 million in 2012, with 2013’s “Catching Fire” as the highest opening with $158 million and an $865 million final global tally. The final two-part “Mockingjay” movies opened with $121 million for “Part One” and $102 million for “Part Two.” “Sunrise on the Reaping” tells the story of young Haymitch Abernathy, played by Woody Harrelson in the original movies and now portrayed by Joseph Zada. He becomes a tribute for the 50th Hunger Games, which brings in twice the number of kids to battle to the death. The movie also stars Mckenna Grace, Ralph Fiennes, Kiernan Culkin, Glenn Close, Elle Fanning, Jesse Plemons and more. full_text: × Nov 20, 2026 8:03am PT Gérard Depardieu Faces New Rape and Sexual Assault Complaint Alongside Director Guillaume Nicloux and Writer Michel Houellebecq By Elsa Keslassy Plus Icon Elsa Keslassy International Correspondent @elsakeslassy Latest Sofia Coppola Pays Tribute to Late Mother Eleanor Coppola at Chanel-Hosted Paris Screening of ‘Making Marie Antoinette’ 2 hours ago Bond Girl Lea Seydoux Says ‘I Don’t Really Care’ Who Becomes 007’s New Female Lead: ‘It’s Become American’ Now 24 hours ago Penelope Cruz to Star in and Produce Netflix Drama ‘Patricia’ From ‘On the Fringes’ Director Juan Diego Botto 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Films du Worso French actor Gérard Depardieu is facing a new complaint alleging rape and sexual assault during the filming of Guillaume Nicloux’s “Thalasso” in 2018, according to an investigation published by Mediapart on Thursday. The complaint also names Nicloux, who directed the film, and Michel Houellebecq, one of France’s most celebrated novelists who starred alongside Depardieu. The alleged incident took place on Dec. 11, 2018, during a scene that was filmed by the movie’s cameras, although the screenplay did not include any sexual activity, according to Mediapart. Related Stories Joshua Jackson Teases ‘Sex, Drugs and Rock 'n' Roll’ in New HBO Max Series ‘How to Survive Without Me’: ‘I'm Getting Too Old For This S---’ ‘La Bola Negra’ to Receive International Star Award at Palm Springs International Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE) The complainant, an actor, alleges that she was raped by Depardieu and sexually assaulted by Houellebecq in the presence of Nicloux, whom she accuses of complicity. Nicloux told Mediapart that he had not witnessed “any coercion, verbal or physical opposition” during the filming of the scene. He said he was distressed to learn that the actor had experienced what she described without his realizing it, and acknowledged having apologized to her afterward. Depardieu’s lawyers, Delphine Meillet and David-Olivier Kaminski, told French radio station RTL that they were unaware of the proceedings. The complaint was filed in May 2025, shortly after Depardieu stood trial for sexually assaulting two women on the set of the 2021 film “Les Volets verts.” The new allegations come just days after Depardieu withdrew his appeal against his conviction in that case, making his 18-month suspended prison sentence final. In a statement titled “J’entends” (“I Hear”) released Monday, the 77-year-old actor accepted responsibility for his conviction and offered “deep and sincere apologies” to those who “may have suffered as a result.” “Justice has spoken. I have been found guilty. I accept this and take responsibility for this conviction,” Depardieu wrote, according to Le Monde. His lawyer, Meillet, said the actor had undergone a period of reflection and wanted to avoid putting the complainants through another trial. “He is a man who has come a long way, who has reached a turning point, who has taken a big step after a long period of reflection and maturation,” Meillet said. “He wanted to avoid making the complainants go through another hearing, or having to go through one himself.” Depardieu also faces a separate rape case involving actress Charlotte Arnould, who accused him of assaulting her in 2018. An investigating judge has ordered the actor to stand trial, a decision he is contesting. The Paris appeals court is expected to rule on Nov. 26 on whether the case will proceed to trial. title: Don’t Tell Comedy & Cash App Partner On Slate Of Half-Hour Stand-Up Specials

Major platforms such as Comedy Central once backed them consistently as a way to break new talent. But with this kind of institutional support waning in recent years, Don’t Tell has partnered with Cash App to help fill the gap. The companies have partnered on The DTC x Cash App Half-Hours , which Kusher said will “elevate fan-favorite comedians from past Don’t Tell tapings for an extended set.” They’ve produced a slate of 12 short specials, the first of which, from comedian Adam Gilbert, premieres on Don’t Tell’s YouTube page today. Related Stories News Banijay & Don’t Tell Comedy Strike Strategic Partnership News Gabriel Iglesias Sets Fifth Netflix Special ‘Lone Star Fluffy’ For Christmas Eve Release New half-hours will be released each week through February 2027. The rest of the lineup features Brittany Lyseng, Calvin Evans, Danny Jolles, Fumi Abe, Ian Lara, Kat Bird, Laurie Kilmartin, Mary Santora, Paris Sashay, Sean Grant, and Shaunak Godkhindi, with three bonus specials from Jay Larson, Zain Sharif, and Chloe Radcliffe. These half-hour specials give comics more room to show what they can do and audiences a chance to discover their next favorite comedian.” Founded by Kyle Kazanjian-Amory in a Los Angeles backyard in 2017, Don’t Tell Comedy has come to be recognized as one of our most important current incubators of rising comedic talent. The company stages more than 5,000 secret-location shows worldwide each year, with taped sets that draw more than 1.5 billion views annually across social channels that have amassed 14 million followers since launching in 2022. Comics who got their start on Don’t Tell stages include Ralph Barbosa, Robby Hoffman, Shapel Lacey, Katherine Blanford and Malik Elassal, to name a few. The company struck a strategic partnership with Banijay America in October, as we first reported.
